approach: Add one cap-budget check and apply it at both pre-dispatch points the request names, a reading and a plan. (1) admission.rs gets `cap_shortfall(texts, base)`, which holds the single text parser `proposed_caps`. It reads proposed `reader_usd`, `producer_usd`, `verifier_usd`, `job_usd`, `planner_usd`, `critic_usd`, `max_rounds` and `[job_plan] enabled` values from sentences that name athena.toml, `[budget]` or `[job_plan]`. It overlays them by plain assignment on a clone of the job's own base `Config` and calls `Config::check_budget()`. On `ConfigError::BudgetBelowReserve` it returns the `required` figure from that error. It never sums caps (`no_second_sum_of_stage_caps_in_core`, run/tests.rs:12005, forbids it, and criterion 5 wants reuse). Three guards keep it from misreading text (this revision answers findings 5 and 7). (a) A text that starts `Field meaning:` is skipped, because the reader brief (reader.rs:303) requires that assumption to quote the live athena.toml value. (b) A mention equal to the base config's current value is dropped, so a restated live value never cancels a different proposal. (c) A sentence is skipped only when it describes an example, fixture, mock or a test's own copy (`a test sets ...`); a sentence that merely says `cargo test passes` is read. (2) Reading time: `check_cap_budget(reading, config)` in reading.rs is called from `build_reading` (reading.rs:777) right after the acceptance-criteria check (940-942) and raises a `NamedRefusal` with rule `check_cap_budget`, on the same path as `check_reading_size` (822-831): `read_once` stores the refusal and `read_for` rereads once with the text. (3) Plan time: `plan_cap_findings(plan, reading, config)` in admission.rs applies the same parser to the reading's cap texts and then the plan's approach, steps, decision choices and the athena.toml file purpose. It returns one Major Athena finding naming `$N.NN`, added at the single call site run/planning.rs:500 so the planner is sent back before any critic call. (4) Tests: each of the four named files pins the cap values in its own helper, so a job_usd-only change needs no test edit. Two shared helpers outside them (`repo_with_config_and_models` in run/tests.rs, `test_config()` in athena-cli tests/common/mod.rs) get the same pin because tests there assert figures against job_usd 50.00 (run/tests.rs:2535, 2607, 10545-10721; drain.rs:5449 asserts `(2.0, 50.0)`). athena.toml gets no net change; the producer raises job_usd to 60.00 once to run the whole suite and reverts it. A table-driven `cap_side` module in refusal_corpus.rs holds the input forms with ids and sources. CHANGELOG.md records the change and D190 is appended to docs/decisions.md.

decisions.choice: 3. One parser in admission.rs, scoped by sentence, with three guards against misreading text. Sentences split on newline, `;` and `.` followed by whitespace or end. A sentence is read only if it names `athena.toml`, `[budget]` or `[job_plan]` (case-insensitive) and is not an example sentence. Example sentence (answers finding 7): any token starting `fixture`, `example`, `hypothet`, `illustrat`, `mock`, `sample`, `instance`, `temporar` or `revert`, or the token `test`/`tests` immediately followed by `set`, `sets`, `write`, `writes`, `use`, `uses`, `build`, `builds`, `feed`, `feeds`, `copy`, `copies`, `config`, `configuration`, `file`, `case`, `input`, `assert` or `asserts`. A bare `test` (`cargo test passes`, `the test suite`) does not exclude a sentence, so 'After athena.toml raises producer_usd to 20.00, cargo test passes' is read and refused, and 'A test sets producer_usd = 99 in a copy of athena.toml' is skipped. Quote guards (answers finding 5): (a) a text whose trimmed form starts `Field meaning` (case-insensitive) is skipped whole, inside `cap_shortfall`, so the corpus and the reading path share it; (b) after collecting mentions in order, any mention equal to the base config's current value (within half a cent; exact for `max_rounds` and `enabled`) is dropped, then the last remaining mention of each key wins. Forms after a key (a key with an identifier character on either side is not a key): `key = N`, `key: N`, `key to N`, `key at N`, `key from A to N`, `key A -> N`, with optional `$` and backticks; values positive; `max_rounds` a whole number; `enabled = true|false` only in a sentence that names `job_plan`. `planner_usd`, `critic_usd`, `max_rounds` and `enabled` are overlaid only when the base config has `[job_plan]`. The refusal text gives the required job_usd as `$N.NN`, the job_usd it was judged against, the shortfall, the exact values read, and the repair (raise job_usd in the same change or lower a cap; describe an example in a sentence that says fixture or example).
decisions.reason: A Reading has no structured field for proposed config values (records.rs:444-482), so text is the only source, and a schema change would hit the reader prompt budget (docs/system-facts.md: reader 1998 of 2000). Finding 5 is real: reader.rs:303 requires every reused config key to carry a `Field meaning:` assumption with 'config: live athena.toml value', and this job's own reading has one ('live athena.toml line 47 job_usd = 50.00'). Without (a) and (b) a summary that raises producer_usd and job_usd would end with job_usd 50.00 (last mention wins) and be refused twice, which fails the job (`read_for`, reading.rs:541-577), and a quoted live producer_usd = 10.00 would cancel a proposed raise. With (a) the mandated quote is never read; with (b) a restatement elsewhere (a summary or criterion) cannot override a different proposal. The check fails open: any unread wording falls back to the candidate-time check (admission.rs:929-958). `budget_required` (config.rs:936-942) counts rounds only when `job_plan.enabled`, so `enabled` changes the figure and is overlaid. The scan test (run/tests.rs:11826-12042) allows plain assignment of cap fields but forbids `+` over them and any call of `planning_usd`, `run_usd`, `critic_usd` or `budget_required` outside `budget_reserve`; `check_budget` (config.rs:948) is not on that list and its `BudgetBelowReserve { job_usd, required, short }` error carries the figure. The error type is `athena_data::config::ConfigError` (the `config` module is imported at admission.rs:23).

risks.risk: The parser misses a wording a reader or planner uses, so an over-budget reading or plan is accepted.
risks.mitigation: The check fails open: an unread wording falls to the candidate-time check (admission.rs:929-958), which is today's behavior. The forms are listed in decision 3 and each has a test and a corpus case. How often readers use another form (prose such as 'raise the producer cap to twelve dollars', or 'reader_usd and producer_usd to 12') is not measured.

risks.risk: A false refusal: a sentence quotes an old or hypothetical figure (such as 'was producer_usd = 80.00 in athena.toml') and the overlay pushes the sum over job_usd. A second refusal is the job's failure (`read_for`, reading.rs:541-577).
risks.mitigation: Only sentences that name athena.toml, [budget] or [job_plan] are read; `Field meaning:` texts are skipped; a mention equal to the base value is dropped, so a restated live value cannot override a proposal (finding 5); example, fixture, mock, sample, temporary and revert sentences and 'a test sets ...' sentences are skipped, while 'cargo test passes' is read (finding 7); the last remaining mention wins; the refusal text prints the exact values read and says how to restate, and one reread follows. Plans are read only in approach, steps, choices and the athena.toml purpose. The expected share of refusals is about 1% (an estimate, not measured). A stale quote that differs from the base and sits outside a `Field meaning:` text is still read.

risks.risk: Pinning budget values in test helpers could hide a real mismatch between the live athena.toml and its own caps.
risks.mitigation: Keep `the_live_config_covers_its_own_caps` (config.rs), `the_shipped_config_covers_its_own_caps` (reading.rs) and the existing `parsing_configuration_and_untouched_configuration_add_no_violation` (admission.rs:2044), which assert `check_budget().is_ok()` on the live file and no value.

demonstrations.method: Four tests, all named with `cap_budget_refuses`, plus the corpus module. (a) reading.rs: `Athena::build_reading` is given a reader output whose deliverables are athena.toml (modify) and CHANGELOG.md and whose criterion reads `athena.toml raises producer_usd to 20.00`, under the pinned config (required 47.00, job_usd 50.00). It must fail with a `NamedRefusal` of rule `check_cap_budget` whose text contains `$57.00`. The expected figure is computed in the test by assigning producer_usd = 20.0 on a clone and calling `Config::budget_required()`, so the logic is not in the double. A second case lowers job_usd to 40.00 and expects `$47.00`. A third case is the wording 'After athena.toml raises producer_usd to 20.00, cargo test passes' and is refused (finding 7). (b) run_pin_tests.rs: `Athena::ask` with a `reader_proposing_caps` tweak (deliverables athena.toml, first criterion `athena.toml raises producer_usd to 60.00`) on the pinned `config(true)`; attempt 1 is recorded with rule `check_cap_budget` and a text naming `$67.00` (reader 2 + producer 60 + verifier 5), attempt 2 is accepted, the reader ran twice. (c) admission.rs: `plan_cap_findings` on a plan whose athena.toml file purpose says `raise producer_usd to 20.00` returns one Major Athena finding at `files, athena.toml` naming `$57.00`. (d) run/tests.rs `plan_cap_budget_refuses_a_plan_over_job_usd_before_the_critic`: `repo_with_planning(3)`; the reader output is rewritten (as `run_planned_behavior` does, 1379-1387) so deliverables[0] is athena.toml (modify) and the criterion reads `athena.toml is changed as the request describes` (names the file, no cap value, so the reading-time check passes and the governance rule is satisfied); first plan is `good_plan()` with files athena.toml and approach/purpose `Raise producer_usd to 60.00 in athena.toml.`; second plan keeps athena.toml with purpose `Keep the caps as they are.` The test asserts the second planner brief contains the finding and the figure computed in the test (parse the repo's athena.toml, assign producer_usd = 60.0, call `budget_required()`; 2 + 3 x 1.50 + 60 + 5 = 71.50), contains no governance-listing finding, and that the critic's first brief is for the revised plan and not for the first. The corpus module `cap_side` (step 11) drives `cap_shortfall` on the same shapes with real sources.
